entries.gave: Read the Cut, invoicer as it stands (lines, totals, tax, render, command, tests, pyproject 1.5.0) and the one More kept. Its people: colleagues from accounting, who run the invoicer command on the lines saved from their spreadsheet at the client's rate, and the maintainers and code that call the package's subtotal and total, who are after the same figures the invoice prints. The More: totals.total and render read their lines twice, so a generator gives a total without tax.
Read best-practices/code/best-practice.md with its template.md, and best-practices/refactor-code/best-practice.md, to their end, before any change.

Decided: take each decision of the Cut as it stands; settle that subtotal, tax, total and render take Iterable[Line] read once (total reckons the subtotal once and adds tax_of of it; render lists its lines once), as the decision asks that the printed invoice and the package give the same figures for any iterable; nothing left open for the person.
Took the test command from pyproject.toml: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests.
Ran it in a throwaway copy: 62 tests pass before any change.
Unit cases for the decision: subtotal, tax, total and render each take any iterable of lines, a generator included, and give the figures they give for the same lines as a list.
No new option, mode or branch: total reckons the subtotal once and adds tax_of of it, and render takes its lines into a list once, as it reads them for the rows and the sums.
The reckoning of subtotal, tax and total stays only in invoicer/totals.py; render keeps calling it, and tax_of and to_cent stay in tax.py.

Added four tests in tests/test_totals.py, one per case: test_subtotal_of_a_generator_of_lines_adds_its_amounts, test_tax_of_a_generator_of_lines_is_that_of_its_subtotal, test_total_of_a_generator_of_lines_adds_the_tax, test_render_of_a_generator_of_lines_prints_their_subtotal_and_total.

Ran the new tests before the body changed: total of a generator failed with 20.00 != 23.80, and render of a generator printed Subtotal 0, the reasons their Then names; subtotal and tax already read once and pass, pinning that.
Least code: totals.total reckons the subtotal once and adds tax_of of it; render reads its lines into a list once. 66 tests pass.
Docstrings of subtotal, tax, total and render say the lines may be any iterable, a generator included, read once; type hints of subtotal, tax and total are Iterable[Line].
Ran the 66 tests three times in shuffled orders, seeds 1, 2 and 3, each OK.

coverage.py is not installed in the throwaway copy, so line coverage was taken with python3 -m trace --count --missing over the test run: no line of invoicer/totals.py or invoicer/render.py goes unrun.
After the change of totals.total and of render, the 66 tests pass; every behavior of a list of lines holds, and a generator now gives what 1.4.0 gave for total, 23.80 for 20.00 at 19 percent.
render.py: comment beside lines = list(lines) says why, as the rows and each sum read the lines.

invoicer/totals.py: subtotal, tax, total take Iterable[Line], total reckons the subtotal once; invoicer/render.py reads its lines into a list once; tests/test_totals.py gains four generator tests; 66 pass.

Installed the package by pip from the repository in a throwaway copy and ran invoicer lines.csv --rate 19: the invoice prints, exit 0; --rate 0.19 is refused with the message to write the percent, exit 2.

Tried in a throwaway copy: installed invoicer prints the two-line invoice at 19 percent (Total 250.50, exit 0) and refuses --rate 0.19 (exit 2); a Python caller passing a generator of one 20.00 line gets subtotal 20.00, total 23.80, and render prints Subtotal 20.00, Tax 3.80, Total 23.80 (exit 0). pipx and venv are absent there, so pip --target stood in for pipx install.
